column2: He made the earth level properly; for we have heard that the earth was greatly uneven.
By the god Vishnu, by Shakra, by the gods and sages, he was consecrated by Brahma for the protection of subjects.
The earth herself served him, Pandava, bringing jewels; the ocean, lord of rivers, and the Himalaya, best of mountains, too.
Shakra gave him inexhaustible wealth, Yudhishthira, and great Meru, the golden mountain itself, gave gold.
And the revered Naravahana (Kubera), lord of Yakshas and Rakshasas, gave wealth fit for dharma, wealth and desire.
Horses, chariots, elephants and crores of men appeared by Vainya's mere thought, Pandava; there was neither old age, famine, poverty nor disease.
No fear from reptiles, thieves, or from one another ever arose there, by that king's protection.
By him this earth was milked for seventeen kinds of grain, and for whatever was desired by Yakshas, Rakshasas and serpents.
By that great soul this world was made foremost in dharma, and all subjects were pleased; therefore he is called raja (king).
Because he protected (trayate) Brahmanas from wounds (kshata), he is called kshatriya; and this earth, spread out (prathita) by him, is remembered by the good as Prithvi.
The eternal Vishnu himself made the establishment: "No one will transgress you, O king."
By austerity the revered Vishnu entered the lord of the earth; the god-like (king), before whom the world bows, among gods and kings, O king.
Protected ever by the rod-policy, O lord of men, no one assailed him, from the constant sight of spies.
By himself and by his instruments, for the whole earth's lord—what other cause is there for which the world should obey, but fate and merit?
From Vishnu's forehead a golden lotus arose, from which the goddess Shri was born, wife of the wise Dharma.
From Shri wealth arose, with dharma, Pandava; thus dharma, wealth and Shri are established in the kingdom.
From the exhaustion of his merit, coming from heaven to earth, a king is born, dear one, following the control of the rod-policy.
On earth a man is joined with Vishnu's greatness; he is joined to intellect and attains greatness.
No one transgresses the establishment of the gods; the world remains under the sway of one, if he is followed.
An auspicious deed, king of kings, is made for auspiciousness for the one, equal to the rest, in whose word this world stays.
One who has seen his face, gentle one, follows his will and sees himself fortunate, wealthy and handsome.
Therefore in the world, king of kings, the wise ever say that gods and kings are equal, lord of men.
All this has been told to you concerning the greatness of kings, entirely, best of the Bharatas; what else should proceed here?"

What are the dharmas of all classes, what separately for the four classes and the four stages of life, and what are held to be the duties of kings?
mahabharata:12:60.3	By what does a kingdom grow, by what does a king grow, and by what do townsfolk and servants grow, bull of the Bharatas?
mahabharata:12:60.4	What kind of treasury, rod, fort, helpers, ministers, priests, household priests and teachers should a king avoid?
mahabharata:12:60.5	In whom should kings trust in any calamity, and whence should the self be firmly guarded? Tell me that, grandsire.

Homage to great dharma, homage to Krishna the Creator; having bowed to the Brahmanas I shall tell the eternal dharmas.
mahabharata:12:60.7	Freedom from anger, truthful speech, sharing, forbearance, begetting offspring on one's own wives, purity and non-malice,
mahabharata:12:60.8	uprightness, supporting dependants: these nine are for all classes. The dharma of the Brahmana I shall tell you separately.
mahabharata:12:60.9	Self-control, great king, they call the ancient dharma; Vedic study and teaching—in these his work is completed.
mahabharata:12:60.11	He should beget offspring, give and sacrifice; wealth is to be enjoyed by the good after sharing, so it is held.
mahabharata:12:60.12	A Brahmana whose duty is complete by Vedic study alone may do something else or not; he is called a friend (maitra) Brahmana.
mahabharata:12:60.13	The dharma of the kshatriya too I shall tell you, Bharata: a king should give and not beg, sacrifice but not officiate,
mahabharata:12:60.14	not teach, but study; protect the subjects, ever active in slaying robbers; he should show valour in battle.
mahabharata:12:60.15	Those kings who have sacrificed with sacrifices and are learned, and those who are conquerors in battle, are the foremost conquerors of the world.
mahabharata:12:60.16	A kshatriya who returns from the battle with an unwounded body—the ancient sages do not praise that deed of his.
mahabharata:12:60.17	The slaying of enemies is called the chief dharma of kshatriyas; for him there is no work more incumbent than the destruction of robbers.
mahabharata:12:60.18	Giving, study, sacrifice, yoga and security are prescribed; therefore a king wishing dharma especially should fight.
mahabharata:12:60.19	Having established all subjects in their own dharmas, the lord of the earth should have all tasks done in accord with dharma.
mahabharata:12:60.20	A king whose duty is complete through protection may do something else or not; he is called an Aindra kshatriya.
mahabharata:12:60.21	The dharma of the Vaishya here I shall tell you, Bharata: giving, study, sacrifice, and gathering wealth by purity.
mahabharata:12:60.22	The Vaishya, devoted, should protect all cattle as a father; any other work he might do would be a wrong deed; by protecting them he would attain great happiness.
mahabharata:12:60.23	For the Prajapati, having created animals, entrusted them to the Vaishya, and entrusted all subjects to the Brahmana and king.
mahabharata:12:60.24	I shall tell his livelihood and what he lives on: from six cows he may drink the milk of one, and from a hundred take a pair.
mahabharata:12:60.25	In case of loss, a seventh part; and from the horn a part, from the hoof a part; for grain and all seeds, this is the yearly wage.
mahabharata:12:60.26	The Vaishya should have no thought, I will not protect cattle"; if the Vaishya wishes it, they are not to be protected by another in any way.
The dharma of the Shudra too I shall tell you, Bharata: the Prajapati made the Shudra a servant of the classes.
Therefore service of the classes is prescribed for the Shudra, and by serving them he would attain great happiness.
A Shudra should serve these three classes without envy, and a Shudra should never make accumulations in any way.
For the lowly, obtaining wealth, would bring the greater under his sway; or, permitted by the king, the righteous one may do as he wishes.
I shall tell his livelihood and what he lives on: the Shudra is called one to be necessarily supported by the classes.
Umbrella, turban, usira, sandals and fans, used ones, are to be given to the serving Shudra.
Worn-out and torn garments of the twice-born are to be given to the Shudra; that is his wealth of dharma.
Any Shudra who comes to serve the twice-born, for him the knowers of dharma prescribe a livelihood; a morsel is to be given to him who has not left, and the aged and weak are to be supported.

A Shudra must not abandon his master in any calamity; he is to be supported even in excess when the master's wealth is lost; for a Shudra has no property of his own, his wealth being what the master takes.
Sacrifice is said to belong to the three classes only, Bharata; for the Shudra the mantras "Svaha" and "Namah" are prescribed.
By those a Shudra, keeping vows, may sacrifice with the household sacrifice himself; the fee of a household sacrifice is called a vessel filled.
We have heard that a Shudra named Paijavana gave a hundred thousand as fee by the Aindragna rite.
Therefore faith in sacrifice is prescribed for all classes; for faith is a great deity and the purifier of sacrificers.
Brahmanas, each with their own supreme deity, in this world sacrificed with sessions for these and those eternal desires.
Creations in the three classes are mixed by Brahmanas alone; what the gods among gods say is supreme; therefore sacrifices are performed by the classes together, not for desire.
A twice-born who knows the Rik, Yajus and Saman is ever to be honoured like a god; one without Rik, Yajus and Saman is an affliction of the Prajapati.
Sacrifice is by thought, dear one, in all classes, Bharata; the gods do not strive against it nor do other people; therefore faith in sacrifice is prescribed for all classes.
The Brahmanas have their own deity and always sacrificed to the other classes thus; that great dharma, created by Brahma, was seen to please us in the three classes.
Therefore the classes, upright, are joined in the dharmas of their births; this is its fruit: one Saman, one Yajus, one Rik, one Brahmana; no doubt was seen among them.
On this the ancients recite songs on sacrifice, of the Vaikhanasa sages who wished to sacrifice, king of kings:
Whether the sun has risen or not, the faithful, with senses subdued, offers in the fire by dharma; faith is indeed the great cause.
What is spilled is the former, what is unspilled the latter; sacrifice has many forms and various fruits of works.
The twice-born who knows these, established by certainty of knowledge, endowed with faith, is fit to sacrifice.
Whether a thief or a sinner or the greatest of sinners, he who wishes to sacrifice a sacrifice, they call him good.
The sages praise him, and that is surely good; in every way sacrifice is to be performed by all classes, so it is settled; for there is nothing equal to sacrifice in the three worlds.
Therefore they say it should be performed by a man without envy, relying on faith as purifier, giving according to ability."

The forest-dweller, the life of alms, the householder's great stage, and the celibate student's stage are called the fourth, chosen by Brahmanas.
mahabharata:12:61.3	Having obtained twice-born status by the rite of matted hair, having performed rites beginning with the installation of fires and studied the Veda,
mahabharata:12:61.4	with wife or without, self-possessed, with senses restrained, having done his task, let him go from the householder's stage to the forest stage.
mahabharata:12:61.5	There, having studied the forest scriptures, the knower of dharma, a celibate, having begotten offspring, goes to union with the imperishable.
mahabharata:12:61.6	These very rites of sages who are celibate are to be done here by a wise Brahmana first, O king.
mahabharata:12:61.7	For a Brahmana who has practised celibacy, authority over the life of alms is praised here for one seeking liberation.
mahabharata:12:61.8	Where he sleeps when the sun sets, without fire, without home, living on what he gets, a sage, self-controlled, with senses subdued,
mahabharata:12:61.9	without hope, equal to all, enjoying nothing, unchanging, the Brahmana, having reached the stage of security, goes to union with the imperishable.
mahabharata:12:61.12	Self-controlled, attentive in oblations to gods and ancestors, ever a giver of food to the twice-born, free of envy, a giver of all signs, and with the three fires, he should be a householder.
mahabharata:12:61.13	On this the great sages, of great power, recite a song of Narayana, of great meaning, joined to excess austerity; hear it as I tell it:
mahabharata:12:61.14	Truth and uprightness, honouring guests, dharma, wealth and delight in one's wife: these pleasures are to be pursued in the world, here and hereafter—this is my view.
mahabharata:12:61.15	Supporting sons and wives and completing the Vedas: the great sages call this the best stage of the good.
mahabharata:12:61.16	A Brahmana who, devoted to sacrifice, dwells in the householder's life as it should be, having rightly purified the householder's livelihood, gains a pure fruit in heaven.
mahabharata:12:61.17	After he leaves the body, his desires, held to be inexhaustible, attend him endlessly, with eyes, heads and mouths on every side.
mahabharata:12:61.18	Eating alone, reciting alone, going alone, Yudhishthira, serving a single teacher, with dirt and mud on him,
mahabharata:12:61.19	the celibate student, keeping vows, ever initiated, self-controlled, doing his duty without questioning the Veda, should always dwell.
mahabharata:12:61.20	Constantly serving his teacher and bowing to him, not abstaining from the six duties yet not engaged in them everywhere,
mahabharata:12:61.21	he does not act by authority, nor serve his enemy; this, dear one, is held to be the stage of the celibate student.

Four stages of life are prescribed for a Brahmana, lord; the three classes follow them, best of the Bharatas.
mahabharata:12:62.3	Many duties have been told, O king, leading to heaven, O kshatriya; these are not remembered in the rule of example; in the kshatriya dharma everything is prescribed fully.
mahabharata:12:62.4	A Brahmana who follows kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra works is blamed in this world, dull-minded, and goes to hell in the next.
mahabharata:12:62.5	The designation prescribed in the world for a slave, a dog, a wolf and an animal, apply to a Brahmana who remains in wrong deeds, Pandava.
mahabharata:12:62.6	For a Brahmana engaged in the six duties in all four stages, endowed with all dharmas, well born and self-controlled,
mahabharata:12:62.7	purified, delighting in austerity, free of hope and generous, the worlds are called imperishable.
mahabharata:12:62.8	Whoever does what work, of what kind, with what and where, in just such a way does he obtain the corresponding quality.
mahabharata:12:62.9	You ought to know, king of kings, the great (matters of) increase, agriculture, trade, livelihood, Vedic study and calculation.
mahabharata:12:62.10	Time, urged by Time, fixed in the turn of Time, helplessly performs works high, low and middle.
mahabharata:12:62.11	Gifts end, and the things that bring good in the past; the world, devoted to its own deeds, is imperishable and many-faced.

Brahma and the six duties are to be served by the wise householder; for a Brahmana who has done his task, dwelling in the forest is praised.
mahabharata:12:63.3	Serving a king, living by agriculture and wealth, and livelihood by trade, crookedness, dealings with dogs and usury should be avoided.
mahabharata:12:63.4	A Brahmana-in-name becomes a Shudra, O king, who is ill-behaved, fallen from dharma, a husband of a low woman, a slanderer, a dancer, a servant of a village, one who does wrong deeds.
mahabharata:12:63.5	One who recites the Vedas and one who does not, O king, equal to Shudras, and to be fed like a slave—all these become equal to Shudras; avoid them at rites for the gods.
mahabharata:12:63.6	Toward one who is unbounded in eating, cruel in conduct, violent, and has abandoned his own dharma and livelihood, oblations, offerings to ancestors and other gifts become undeserved.
mahabharata:12:63.7	Therefore dharma is prescribed for a Brahmana: self-control, purity and uprightness, O king; and all the stages of life for a Brahmana were sent forth by Brahma long ago.
mahabharata:12:63.8	He who is self-controlled, a soma-drinker, of noble conduct, compassionate, tolerant of all, free of hope, upright, gentle, kind and forbearing is a true Brahmana, not another, who does sinful deeds.
mahabharata:12:63.9	The Shudra, Vaishya and prince, O king—all worlds depend on them, wishing dharma; therefore Vishnu, regarding the classes as attached to the dharmas of their birth, does not wish otherwise, Pandava.
mahabharata:12:63.13	For one who has gone a little distance or even for one who has gone ten dharma-ways, all stages are prescribed except the hopeless.
mahabharata:12:63.14	They do not call the life of alms the dharma for him; likewise for the Vaishya, king of kings, and for the prince.
mahabharata:12:63.15	One who has done his task and passed his years, the Vaishya who has laboured for the king, may go, with the king's permission, to the circle of hermitages.
mahabharata:12:63.16	Having studied the Vedas by dharma and the king's sciences, blameless one, having performed rites beginning with offspring and used soma,
mahabharata:12:63.17	having protected all subjects by dharma, best of speakers, and the sacrifices such as the Rajasuya and Ashvamedha and others,
mahabharata:12:63.18	having brought together as taught and given fees to Brahmanas, having obtained victory in battle, whether little or much,
mahabharata:12:63.19	having established a son in the kingdom as protector of subjects, Pandava—whether of another lineage, or one praised, bull among kshatriyas,
mahabharata:12:63.20	having rightly honoured ancestors with ancestral sacrifices by rule, gods with sacrifices and sages with the Vedas with effort,
mahabharata:12:63.21	and when the end comes, whoever wishes another stage, going through the stages in order, O king, attains perfection.
mahabharata:12:63.22	By royal sagehood, O king, by the path of alms-life, though free of household duties, one may move wishing to live.
mahabharata:12:63.23	This is not the final work of the three, bull of the Bharatas; of the four, tiger among kings, they speak of dwellers in stages.
mahabharata:12:63.24	Much depends on kshatriyas, of men, serving the best dharma of the world; all dharmas and sub-dharmas of the three come from the king's dharma, so I hear from the Veda.
mahabharata:12:63.25	As the footprints of all creatures merge into the footprint of an elephant, so all dharmas merge into the duties of kings in every condition; know this.
mahabharata:12:63.26	Those who know dharma say other dharmas have little support and little fruit; the noble say the kshatriya dharma is of great support and of many forms of good, not another.
mahabharata:12:63.27	All dharmas have the duties of kings as chief; all dharmas are protected; all renunciation is in the duties of kings, O king; and in renunciation they say the ancient dharma is chief.
mahabharata:12:63.28	If the rod-policy is slain, the triple learning would sink, and all dharmas would not be in harmony; all the dharmas of the stages of life would go if the kshatriya, the ancient duty of kings, were abandoned.
mahabharata:12:63.29	All renunciations are seen in the duties of kings; all initiations are taught in the duties of kings; all yogas are taught in the duties of kings; all worlds have entered the duties of kings.
mahabharata:12:63.30	As creatures slain in nature are for the torment of those who rely on dharma, so dharmas deprived of the duties of kings, in every condition, do not honour their own dharma.

All these dharmas, best of the Bharatas, are in the kshatriya; in the living world, free of hope, they rest in the kshatriya dharma.
mahabharata:12:64.3	The dharma of those dwelling in stages is imperceptible, of many doors; they describe its nature by the scriptures alone, as eternal.
mahabharata:12:64.4	Others, disputing with holy words about the world's settled truth, ignorant of certainty about dharmas, delight in the unseen end.
mahabharata:12:64.5	Dharma, mostly of visible happiness, witnessed by the self, guileless, beneficial to all the world, is established in kshatriyas.
mahabharata:12:64.6	Of Brahmanas who are engaged in the dharma of stages, Yudhishthira, as for the three classes, there was earlier an account of incomparable duties of kings, praiseworthy in this world by good conduct.
mahabharata:12:64.7	It has been told to you, king of kings, how, long ago, many brave kings went to the greatly radiant Vishnu, the lord of all beings, the lord Narayana, for the rod-policy.
mahabharata:12:64.8	Having weighed each of their own works in a stage of life, the kings of old waited upon him, established in the word of example.
mahabharata:12:64.9	Sadhyas, gods, Vasus and the Ashvins, Rudras, Vishvedevas and hosts of Maruts were created long ago by the First God; the gods and the perfected abide in the kshatriya dharma.
mahabharata:12:64.13	Vishnu showed himself to Vasava in a form; he, surrounded by good kings, worshipped that lord.
mahabharata:12:64.14	There was this great dialogue between that host of kings and that great soul about Vishnu, greatly radiant one.
mahabharata:12:64.15	[The kings said:] What is wished, best of those who uphold dharma, that you wish to see the immeasurable one, of endless illusion and immeasurable might, Narayana, the first god, the ancient?
That god of universal form cannot be seen even by me or by Brahma in person; any other wishes of yours, O king, that are in your heart, I shall give, for you are king among mortals.
Established in truth, devoted to dharma, with senses subdued, brave, firm, delighting in the gods, by your wisdom, devotion and highest faith, I shall therefore give you a boon as you wish."

Without doubt, revered one, I shall see the first god, having pleased him with my head; I wish, abandoning pleasures, desiring dharma, to go to the forest, the good path honoured by the world.
mahabharata:12:64.19	By the vast, immeasurable kshatriya dharma, worlds have been won and one's own fame established; the dharma that proceeds from the first god, the eldest of the world—I do not know how to do it.

Without an army, devoted to dharma, you will roam and attain the supreme goal, careless no more; the kshatriya dharma proceeded from the first god, and the other dharmas are the remainder.
mahabharata:12:64.21	The remainder were created finite; the endless have a good departure, distinguished by the kshatriya dharma; all dharmas have entered this dharma; therefore they call this dharma the best.
mahabharata:12:64.22	By action, of old, gods and sages of immeasurable splendour were all saved, crushing enemies, by Vishnu with kshatriya dharma.
mahabharata:12:64.23	If that revered one, wealthy, immeasurable, had not slain all the enemies, neither Brahmanas nor the creator of the worlds nor good dharmas nor the original dharmas would be.
mahabharata:12:64.24	If that best of gods, of old, immeasurable, had not conquered this earth by valour, the four classes and the dharmas of the four stages would not be, by the destruction of Brahma.
mahabharata:12:64.25	Dharmas were seen in hundreds and, by the eternal kshatriya dharma, were set in motion again; in every age the original dharmas proceed; they call the kshatriya dharma the eldest of the world.
mahabharata:12:64.26	Self-sacrifice, compassion to all beings, knowledge of the world, rescuing and protecting, rescuing the despondent and afflicted: these are in the kshatriya dharma of kings.
mahabharata:12:64.27	Unrestrained men, moved by desire and anger, afraid of kings, do not incur sin; and others, the good, endowed with all dharma, of good conduct, practise good dharma.
mahabharata:12:64.28	All beings in the world, protected by kings as sons by the law of signs, move about; of this there is no doubt.
mahabharata:12:64.29	The kshatriya is devoted to all dharma, eldest of the world, eternal, ever extending to the imperishable, imperishable and many-faced.

Let the king know the refinement of the earth, the union with the kings' rites, non-begging, protection of subjects, compassion for all beings, and giving up the body in battle as the best dharma.
mahabharata:12:65.3	The sages say renunciation is the best; he who gives up the body is best of all; all is always renounced in the duties of kings; these kings are always evidently so.
mahabharata:12:65.4	By great learning, by serving a teacher, or by striking another, they ever say a kshatriya celibate, devoted to dharma, should walk the stage alone.
mahabharata:12:65.5	In dealings for common aims, avoiding liked and disliked with care, by establishing the four classes and protecting them, by various means, restraints and by his own;
mahabharata:12:65.6	by all efforts they call the stage dharma; the kshatriya is the eldest, endowed with all dharma. The classes that do not follow their own dharma, to them they speak various dharmas incorrectly.
mahabharata:12:65.7	Those ruined by wealth for unbounded desire they call men turned into beasts; one leads by policy from greed for wealth; therefore the kshatriya dharma is the better stage.
mahabharata:12:65.8	The course of the Brahmanas of the three Vedas and the stage that is declared for Brahmanas—that work they call the best for a Brahmana; doing another, he is liable to the sword like a Shudra.
mahabharata:12:65.9	The dharmas of the four stages and the dharmas of the Veda, O king, are to be followed by the Brahmana; another could not know them in any way.
mahabharata:12:65.11	A Brahmana who remains in wrong deeds does not deserve honour; they hold him untrustworthy who is not employed in works.
mahabharata:12:65.12	These dharmas and all classes are to be raised by heroic kshatriyas; this is the dharma; therefore the duties of kings are the eldest and none other; those heroic dharmas that are eldest in valour are so held.
mahabharata:12:65.13	Yavanas, Kiratas, Gandharas, Chinas, Shabaras, Barbaras, Shakas, Tusharas, Kahvas, Pahlavas, Andhras, Madrakas,
Odras, Pulindas, Ramathas, Kachas, and Mlecchas everywhere, and those born of Brahmanas and kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, among men:
how should they all, living in the realm, practise dharma, and how are they all, who live by robbery, to be established by men like me?
I wish to hear this; tell it to me, revered one, for you are like a kinsman to us kshatriyas, lord of the gods."

Service of mother and father is to be done by all robbers, and service of teachers and of dwellers in stages.
mahabharata:12:65.18	Service of lords of the earth must be done by all robbers, and rites of Vedic dharma are prescribed for them.
mahabharata:12:65.19	Ancestral sacrifices, wells, water-sheds, beds and gifts they should give to the twice-born at the proper time.
mahabharata:12:65.20	Non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, protecting the inheritance of livelihood, supporting sons and wives, purity and non-malice are for them.
[Death said:] "Whatever activities there are here are all urged by Time; this I said before, hunter, because of Time."
His son was born of Prajati, famed as Kshupa, and Kshupa's son Ikshvaku became a lord of the earth.
The two sons of Madri, knowing Bhima's mind, approved, and guarding the king's feelings, said nothing unpleasant.
Then a great drinking-feast began at Prabhasa, of those of keen splendour, thronged with hundreds of instruments, filled with actors and dancers.
[Vaishampayana said:] Having said this, the king went on, and Bhima fell; and fallen, Bhima said to Yudhishthira, king of dharma:
He heard those voices again and again, as before, of the weary and the grieved, and the Pandava did not recognise them.
